review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the ProjectiveSpace/Charts.lean declarations it relies on (projectiveSpaceHomogeneousCoordinate, its `_def`, `_self` and `_injective` lemmas) and Mathlib's NormedSpace.normalize lemma set. The file's simp interface is small. `projectiveSpaceHomogeneousVector_apply` is @[simp] and proved by rfl. Its right-hand side is a different head symbol (`projectiveSpaceHomogeneousCoordinate`), so I see no cycle. The upstream `projectiveSpaceHomogeneousCoordinate_self` is already @[simp] and covers the `j = k` case, and `vectorChart_coordinate` uses it through `simp [hk]`. The private rfl lemmas (`projectiveSpaceHomeomorph_symm_apply`, `projectivePoint_mk`) are used only through targeted `rw`, so leaving them out of simp is defensible. They would also expose the private `projectivePoint`/`spherePoint` to simp. The one smell is that `homogeneousSphere_ratio` unfolds `NormedSpace.normalize` with a non-terminal `simp` and then `field_simp`. I found no concrete missing simp lemma or bad orientation that would be better, and I can't run Lean to check how brittle that proof is. Mathlib already has the relevant @[simp] lemmas for `normalize`. I found nothing that justified a finding under this rubric. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not check downstream files for uses of the public comparison lemmas. A grep outside this file found no uses of `projectiveSpaceHomeomorph` or `projectiveSpaceHomogeneousVector`.
